newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Lotus expected to announce Proton deal.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Lotus expected to announce Proton deal.

text.p: Britain's Group Lotus Ltd was expected to confirm Malaysia's Proton as conference at its headquarters in Norfolk, eastern England later on Wednesday, and has already said it is working on technical collaboration with Proton.

Lotus's Italian owner Romano Artioli has been seeking a new partner to take up a stake in the automotive engineer and sportscar maker for much of this year, and newspaper reports said Proton was likely to take a stake of 80 percent.
In mid-September Artioli promised his staff he would announce a new partner for Lotus "within days".

By early October, however, Daewoo, the only company to have confirmed that it was actually in talks to buy Lotus, said negotiations had broken down as the two parties had failed to narrow their differences.

And in Seoul on Wednesday, Daewoo spokesman Lee Chang-won told Reuters, "We have not talked to Lotus for several months over any acquisition. We had earlier sought to take over the company but the idea has been shelved."
The newspaper reports say the Proton stake would cost around $100 million including assumption of debt.
Artioli owns Lotus via the Luxembourg-registered Bugatti International SA group, which in turn is the parent of the Italian car company Bugatti Automobili which went into receivership last year.

Started by motor racing engineer Colin Chapman in the early 1950s, Lotus was once a leading name in Grand Prix racing, winning world championships with drivers Graham Hill, Jim Cled up losses of 50 million pounds ($75 million) in the five years before its sale in 1993 to Bugatti International.
